title: Output damage from ablating each lens's direction
takeaway: Zeroing the residual-stream component along a lens's vector for the intermediate concept moves the model's output distribution further when that vector comes from the Jacobian lens than when it comes from the logit lens or the tuned lens, on all three prompt distributions shown. On the multihop set the J-lens ablation induces roughly twice the KL divergence of the other two. The paper reads this as evidence that the J-lens direction is the one the model actually computes with, not merely the one that displays the concept.
walkthrough:
A grouped bar chart. The x-axis carries three prompt distributions from the paper's [[intermediate-concept-benchmarks]]: the [[multihop-benchmark]], the [[multilingual-benchmark]] and the [[poetry-benchmark]]. Within each group stand three bars, one per lens, keyed by the legend titled "Lens Type": black for the [[jacobian-lens]], red for the [[logit-lens]], blue for the [[tuned-lens]]. Bar height is the mean [[kl-divergence]] induced on the model's output distribution, averaged over the items in that benchmark.

The intervention behind a single bar runs as follows. Every lens assigns each vocabulary token a direction in the [[residual-stream]] — for the J-lens this is the [[j-lens-vector]]. Each benchmark item has a known intermediate concept the model must compute but never sees and never says, such as Mars in "the color of the planet fourth from the Sun is". The lens's vector for that intermediate token is taken, and the residual stream's component along it is projected to zero. The KL divergence between the resulting output distribution and the undisturbed one is recorded. This is the paper's [[ablation-kl-effect]]. A larger value means the erased direction mattered more to the answer.

The caption states that the projection is applied at all positions, with the poetry items excluded at the target position — the place where the rhyme word itself is produced. The body text of the same section instead describes ablating at the readout position; the caption is the more specific statement for this chart.

Reading the heights, the black bar is the tallest in every group. Multihop shows the widest gap: about $2.12$ for the J-lens against about $0.93$ and $0.88$, the "roughly twice" the text reports. Multilingual gives $0.91$, $0.67$ and $0.48$. Poetry gives $0.59$, $0.23$ and $0.34$, and there the tuned lens edges above the logit lens.

The error bars carry the qualification. On multihop and multilingual the black interval clears both others. On poetry it overlaps the tuned-lens interval, so the ordering within that group is not separated by this measure. The figure also does not label what the bars represent, and it covers three of the six distributions. The companion evidence is the [[swap-success-rate]], reported separately.

terms.definition: The vertical axis: the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the model's next-token distribution after the ablation and its distribution without the ablation, averaged over the items of one benchmark. Larger means the ablation disturbed the output more.
The legend key: which of the three interpretability methods supplied the direction that was ablated. Colour, not position, identifies the lens.
The paper's own method, which assigns each vocabulary token the residual-stream direction that disposes the model toward saying that token. Its bar is the black one in each group.
An earlier method that decodes an intermediate residual-stream state by applying the model's final unembedding to it directly. Its token direction is simply the corresponding unembedding row.

A method that trains a per-layer affine map so that the decoded distribution matches the model's own final output distribution. Its objective is agreement with the output rather than exposure of intermediates.
The benchmark of two-hop factual questions where the model must compute a bridging entity, for example computing Mars before answering "red". Fifty items.
The benchmark of prompts written entirely in a non-English language, testing whether the model routes through English-aligned representations. Fifty-four items, each with four intermediates.
The benchmark of rhyming couplets where the intermediate is the final word of the second line, sought at the newline between the lines. Fifty-two items.

The lens's vector for the token naming the item's known intermediate concept — the thing ablated in this experiment. Each lens supplies a different vector for the same token, which is what the chart compares.
The intervention that removes the residual stream's component along a chosen direction while leaving the rest of the activation untouched. Here it is applied to the intermediate direction.
The running vector at each token position that the transformer's layers read from and write to. It is the space in which every lens vector lives and in which the ablation is performed.
In the poetry items, the position at which the rhyme word is produced. The caption says ablation is applied at all positions except this one for poetry.
The vertical whiskers on each bar, marking the spread around the mean across items. The figure does not state what they represent.
The paper's name for the quantity plotted: the causal metric measuring how much the output moves when a lens's intermediate direction is removed.
The second causal metric in the same comparison, reported in the next figure rather than here: how often exchanging one intermediate for another flips the model's top-1 output.

numbers.meaning: The range of the y-axis. It is set by the tallest bar, the multihop J-lens value near 2.12; every other bar sits below 1.0.

Multihop, Jacobian lens: the mean KL divergence from ablating the J-lens direction for the bridging entity. The largest effect in the figure, and the basis for the text's claim of roughly twice the other lenses.
Multihop, logit lens. Ablating the unembedding direction for the same intermediate token moves the output less than half as far as the J-lens direction does.
Multihop, tuned lens. Close to the logit-lens value, and likewise far below the J-lens bar.
Multilingual, Jacobian lens. The J-lens again leads its group, though the whole group sits much lower than multihop.
Multilingual, logit lens. Second in its group, above the tuned lens.
Multilingual, tuned lens. The smallest of the three in this group, and the tightest error bar in the figure.
Poetry, Jacobian lens. The leading bar of the group, but with a wide error bar.
Poetry, logit lens. The smallest bar in the whole figure. The poetry readout sits at a newline, a position where next-token-aligned directions carry little of the planned rhyme.
Poetry, tuned lens. The one place in the figure where the tuned lens exceeds the logit lens.
The J-lens interval clears both others with a gap, so the ordering in this group is not explained by item-to-item spread.
All three intervals are disjoint, giving the cleanest three-way separation in the figure.
The J-lens interval overlaps the tuned-lens interval, so the J-lens advantage over the tuned lens is not separated here. It does clear the logit-lens interval.
The paper's summary of the multihop gap. The arithmetic: 2.12 divided by 0.93 is about 2.3, and 2.12 divided by 0.88 is about 2.4, so "roughly twice" is a conservative statement of the ratio.
The number of items in the multihop, multilingual and poetry benchmarks respectively, over which each bar's mean is taken. The counts come from the section text, not from the figure.
The chart covers three of the six prompt distributions the section builds. Order of operations, typo and association are not plotted here.
